text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Interior Ministry called 37,000 police to supervise elections on Sunday.
- The ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) will not contest election results, executive leader Adrian Nastase said when casting his vote.
- Election results could be annuled due to high number of ballots with printing errors, head of Central Electoral Bureau told Antenna 1 private television on Sunday.
ADEVARUL
- IMAS and IRSOP exit polls have confirmed pre-electoral opinion polls.
- Tourism ministry's driver was arrested for trying to vote three times for President Ion Iliescu.
- Some 70,000 Romanians or Romanian Jews living in Israel have cast their votes on ballots containing lists of Bucharest candidates.
- Full-page report on how characters involved in the country's biggest fraud and fiscal evasion cases voted in prisons.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- IMAS exit poll released early on Monday put opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) leader Emil Constantinescu ahead in presidential election with 33 percent, with president Ion Iliescu following closely with 31 percent. CDR got some 37 percent and PDSR was estimated to get 24 percent.

- IRSOP exit poll released on Romanian state television soon after polling stations closed at midnight shows Constantinescu trailing with 30 percent while his main rival, President Iliescu, got 33 percent.
- Heavy voting was registered among Romanians living abroad.
- "I expected a bigger loss, given the fact that the government has constantly dropped in popularity in the past years" said Ion Iliescu after the release of exit polls.
- Iliescu hailed the fact the PDSR has remained the strongest party in Romania, as CDR is not a party but an alliance.
- Iliescu is confident he would defeat Emil Constantinescu in the run-off.

- "We stick to our commitments stated during the election campaign as long as an agreement with the CDR will be reached on objectives to follow," Petre Roman said. Roman got some 20 percent of votes and his party, the Social Democratic Union (USD) got 12 percent, according to the IRSOP exit poll.
- Virgil Magureanu, the head of Romania's Intelligence Service told journalists he didn't want to be the service's head after elections.
- Despite Vacaroiu government promising everything was set for elections, general elections were badly organised, newspaper says in full-page report.
LIBERTATEA
- The opposition has won parliamentary polls.
- Denounced by both the opposition and the ruling forces, electoral vote-rigging did not take place.
- Some 3.5 million ballots needed reprinting 48 hours before polling stations opened.
- Turnout stood at 70.45 percent countrywide at 2030 hours on Sunday.
ZIUA
- The democratic opposition will form Romania's first non-communist government.
- Some 30,000 ballots were stolen in the city of Pitesti.
- Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe is concerned about democracy in Romania, especially limitations of freedom of expression, the OSCE says in an open leter to President Iliescu.
- Romanian television to broadcast the U.S. elections live.
- Full-page report on irregularities in the voting procedures, like incorrect voting lists and ballots already stamped.

- Prospective prime minister in a CDR government, senator Radu Vasile, said he was expecting a "velvet revolution" to take place in Romania after the opposition takes over from the old communists in power.
- Vote-rigging was possible due to some one million reserve ballots printed by the government.

- A political agreement between CDR, USD, National Liberal Alliance and the National Centre Union on cooperation in a future government and support for presidential run-off would be signed very soon, Constantinescu said.
- He said the Hungarian democratic Union was another possible partner.
- Man beat his wife at the polling station and tore her ballot, furious that she did not vote Iliescu for president.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Elections were monitored by 238 foreign observers and 72 foreign journalists.
VOCEA ROMANIEI
- Two newly weds in the Transylvanian town of Campia Turzii cast their votes in wedding gowns, saying marriage and vote were equally important.
DIMINEATA
- Opposition CDR and USD have broken the law when they tore apart PDSR electoral posters and distributed leaflets with Emil Constantinescu and Petre Roman after the legal deadline for campaigning.
- A CDR candidate in Iasi distributed partisan leaflets along with 10,000 lei notes to voters.
- The Sunday vote will reveal a stronger PDSR, Adrian Nastase said in interview.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Iliescu does not rule out any alternative for the ruling coalition after elections. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
